sourced from `TradePageDataRepository.indexTickerItemLiveData.value?.price`).
The option bottom-sheet is per-strike and the shared main-page session's
`InstContext` is NOT on this strike, so the estimated-value derive cannot
read the index off the session/`new_minimal` context (no IndexPrice data
source). Producer: `fetch_option_instrument_detail` (async, keyed by the
fetched `detail.uly`). Consumed by `recompute_amount_pop` as the index
override so the "≈ value" pop shows while typing. Empty until it lands.

fields.doc:

`fetch_option_instrument_detail` fetch. The shared session / option biz
`get_biz_info_for_id(inst_id)` frequently MISSES the tapped strike (the
whole reason `fetch_option_instrument_detail` exists), so the per-keystroke
est-value pop derive cannot rely on the biz map for `ct_mult` / `ct_val_ccy`
/ `ct_type` — a miss yields `OptionInstrument::default()` (empty ct_mult →
wrong coin_amt; empty ct_type → CM misclassified). Cache them here so
`recompute_amount_pop_on_handle` builds an accurate InstContext (V1
`getProbablyValue` reads these off `getBizInfoForId`, which on the main
page DOES have the strike). Empty until the detail fetch lands.

`resolveCdKey`. Producer: `recompute_amount_unit_display` (instrument
landing + `refresh_amount_unit`). Empty until the instrument lands.

fields.name: amount_unit_options
fields.doc:

the OKTradeCore-bound `TradeUnitContractAndOptionBottomSheet`). Option has
exactly two rows — COIN (label = instrument coin symbol, V1
`isShowDetailedCoin=true` used by the option panel) and CONTRACT (CDKey
`pr_options_footer_switch_amount` = Zhang/contract). `is_selected` reflects the live
option trade-unit setting. Native renders the sheet purely from this list
(B1: no OKTradeCore / BizInstrument). Producer:
`recompute_amount_unit_display` (instrument landing + `refresh_amount_unit`
+ `on_amount_unit_changed`). Empty until the instrument lands.

fields.name: amount_digit

contract unit -> `sheetDig` (integer Zhang), coin unit -> `contractDig`
(coin decimals). Producer: `recompute_amount_unit_display`. Native consumes
this for both units; zero is a valid integer-only precision and must not be
replaced by a lotSz/quote-digit fallback. 0 until the instrument lands.

user who CLEARS the price is not re-seeded by the next streaming tick
(the bare `price.is_empty()` guard alone refills on every empty tick).

name: on_hidden
doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase).

Distinct from `on_pause`: the Pure host swaps StrategyType panels via
show/hide keep-alive (NOT re-inflate), so a hidden panel does NOT get
Activity-level `onPause`. Native, by contrast, re-inflates a fresh
Fragment per StrategyType, so it shows a blank draft on every order-type
switch. Amount lives in Rust state and survives hide/show, so to mirror
native we clear the input draft (amount + probably/total + seekbar) ONLY
on this hide transition — NOT on `on_pause` (which also fires on app
backgrounding, where native preserves the typed amount).

Kotlin routing: `PureSpotAdvancedLimitFragment.onHiddenChanged(hidden=true)`
calls `on_pause()` (max_avail reset) AND `on_hidden()` (draft clear);
`Fragment.onPause()` (backgrounding) calls only `on_pause()`.

Keeps `price` intact (sibling parity: post-submit + side-switch resets
keep the limit price). Additive action — forward-compatible; existing
bindings that never call it are unaffected.

name: sync_order_type_epoch

rebuilds the whole trade-panel fragment on an order-type change (orderType

fresh (unchecked + empty). V2 is keep-alive, so the panel + this attached
child survive the switch. The Kotlin host polls this once on the panel's
visible/render tick (same timing as the panel interactor's own
`maybe_reset_on_order_type_switch`); it compares the session order-type
generation with the last-seen value:
- sentinel `u64::MAX` (first sync) -> adopt WITHOUT clearing (deeplink-
preset attach is preserved);
- unchanged -> no-op (④ hide/show re-visit preserves the attach);
- changed -> `reset_after_order` (keep the checkbox CHECKED + the simple
by-rate value, clear by-price / advanced) + return `true` so the host
runs `resetTpslAfterOrderSuccess` (box handling, NO uncheck). Native
rebuilds the fragment which re-reads the per-instType checkbox SP + the
global by-rate SP, so an order-type switch is NOT an uncheck / full wipe
(corrected 2026-07-31; earlier `clear_all_tpsl` + uncheck was wrong).
Returns `true` at most once per real order-type switch.

Holds **all** data Native needs to launch the Transfer Activity:

when true, click should toast `pr_trade_transfer_toast_unavailable_notlist`
instead of launching Transfer.

state mutation that affects (side / instrument / probably_value / amount /
trade_quote_ccy / is_new_coin_disabled). Native never recomputes; it only
reads this struct via state push or consumes the matching UxEvent payload.

fields.name: label_ds
fields.doc:
Locale-aware label for the chip. Rust can't produce locale-formatted
dates without Android APIs (`SimpleDateFormat` / `getBestDateTimePattern`),
so `DisplayString::Date` carries the raw `exp_time_ms` + `DateFormat`
hint and Kotlin's `resolve(ctx)` bridge formats via
`TradeTitleUtils.formatEventDateUtc8(...)`.

(mirrors Native `EventContractTitleHelper.formatUpDownPeriodLabel`).
Stk-based chips (ABOVE / HIT / BETWEEN): `Placeholder` — Kotlin composes
the label from `stk` / `cap_stk` / `method` via `formatPeriodChipLabel`.

Consumers should prefer `label_ds` (after `resolve(ctx)`) over `label`
for UPDOWN; stk-based methods keep using the existing `stk`/`cap_stk`
path. The `label` String field stays populated with the Rust-only
"HH:mm" GMT+8 form as a compat fallback.

name: release

Stop-gap teardown (TEMPORARY — target state is the stream APIs,
which need no teardown call).

One idempotent call at host lifecycle end that breaks the
UniFFI handleMap cycle for any registered callback observers,
ends active streams, and stops effects. On Kotlin call BEFORE
`destroy()`. Includes `stop()`.
